Proverbs 31:10: A courageous woman—who will find her? Such a woman is more precious than costly stones.
Proverbs 31:11: Her husband’s heart is confident in her; such a woman will not lack fine spoils.
Proverbs 31:12: For she works good things for her husband throughout her life.
Proverbs 31:13: Spinning wool and flax, she made useful work with her hands.
Proverbs 31:14: She became like a ship trading from afar, and she gathers her livelihood.
Proverbs 31:15: And she rises in the night and gave food to the household and tasks to the maidservants.
Proverbs 31:16: After inspecting a farm she bought it, and from the fruits of her hands she planted an estate.
Proverbs 31:17: Having girded her waist strongly, she braced her arms for work.
Proverbs 31:18: She tasted that working is good, and her lamp is not extinguished throughout the night.
Proverbs 31:19: She stretches her forearms toward profitable things, and braces her hands on a spindle.
Proverbs 31:20: She opened her hands to a needy person and stretched out her wrist to a poor person.
Proverbs 31:21: Her husband is not anxious about those at home when he stays away somewhere, for all those with her are clothed.
Proverbs 31:23: Her husband becomes distinguished in the gates when he sits in council with the elder inhabitants of the land.
Proverbs 31:24: She made linen cloths and sold them, and girdles for the Canaanites.
Proverbs 31:25: She opened her mouth attentively and lawfully and prescribed order for her tongue.
Proverbs 31:27: The occupations of her houses are secure, and she did not eat idle food.
Proverbs 31:28: She opens her mouth wisely and according to law, and her mercy raised up her children, and they became wealthy, and her husband praised her:
Proverbs 31:29: “Many daughters acquired wealth, many did mighty things, but you stand above and have surpassed them all.”
Proverbs 31:30: A woman’s pleasing qualities are false and beauty is vain; for an understanding woman is blessed, and let her praise the fear of the Lord.

Psalms 92:1: For the day before the Sabbath, when the earth has been inhabited; a praise of a song, of David. The Lord reigned, clothed Himself in comeliness; the Lord clothed Himself in power and girded Himself. For He established the inhabited world, which will not be shaken.
Psalms 92:2: Thy throne is ready from then; Thou art from the age.
Psalms 92:3: The rivers lifted up, Lord; the rivers lifted up their voices.
Psalms 92:4: From the voices of many waters, wondrous are the sea’s surges; wondrous on high is the Lord.
Psalms 92:5: Thy testimonies were made very sure; sanctity befits Thy house, Lord, for length of days.
Psalms 127:1: A song of the ascents. Happy are all who fear the Lord, who walk in His ways.
Psalms 127:2: You will eat the labors of your wrists; happy are you, and it will be well with you.
Psalms 127:3: Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the sides of your house; your sons are like newly planted olive trees around your table.
Psalms 127:4: Behold, thus will the person be blessed who fears the Lord.
Psalms 127:5: May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see Jerusalem’s good things all the days of your life.
Psalms 127:6: And may you see sons of your sons. Peace upon Israel.
